title: A Rapid Image-based Bacterial Virulence Assay Using Amoeba
protocol: Add 25 g of LB-Miller mix in 1 L of double-distilled water for LB preparation.
Autoclave the prepared LB liquid medium to sterilize.
Pour 25 mL of molten LB agar into 10 cm-diameter Petri dishes and allow to solidify at room temperature.
Store liquid media at room temperature and agar plates at 4°C.
Mix 1 g of D-glucose, 2 g of peptone, 0.25 g of yeast extract, 4.2 g of KH2PO4, 5.1 g of Na2HPO47H2O, and 25 g of agar in 1 L of ddH2O for GYP plate preparation.
Autoclave the prepared GYP liquid medium to sterilize.
Pour 25 mL of molten GYP agar into 10 cm-diameter Petri dishes and allow to solidify at room temperature.
Store GYP plates at 4°C.
Mix 10 g of peptone, 7 g of yeast extract, 15 g of D-glucose, 0.12 g of Na2HPO47H2O, 1.4 g of KH2PO4, 40 µg of vitamin B12, and 80 µg of Folic acid in 800 mL of ddH2O for PS medium preparation.
Measure the pH of the PS medium using an electronic pH meter calibrated with pH 4 and pH 7 standards if needed.
Adjust the pH to 6.5 by adding either 5 M KOH or 5 M H3PO4 as necessary.
Add ddH2O to adjust the final volume to 1 L for PS medium preparation.
Filter sterilize the prepared PS medium using a 0.22 µm vacuum filter.
Store the sterilized PS medium at 4°C.
Prepare 1 L of 10x Development Buffer Prime (DB') buffer in a glass bottle by adding 3.4 g of KH2PO4, 13.4 g of Na2HPO4 7H2O, and ddH2O to a total volume of 800 mL.
Calibrate an electronic pH meter using pH 4 and pH 7 standards if the pH meter has not been used within a day.
Measure the pH of the buffer using the calibrated electronic pH meter.
Adjust the pH to 6.5 by gently adding either 5 M KOH or 5 M H3PO4 as needed.
Adjust the final volume to 1 L with ddH2O and sterilize by autoclaving.
Store the prepared buffer at room temperature.
Prepare 1x Development buffer (DB) in a glass bottle by mixing 100 mL of 10x DB' buffer, 1 mL of sterilized 2 M MgCl2, and 1 mL of sterilized 1 M CaCl2.
Adjust the final volume to 1 L with ddH2O that has been autoclaved and sterilized.
Store the prepared buffer at room temperature.
Prepare PS:DB medium in a glass bottle by mixing 100 mL of sterilized PS medium, 100 mL of sterilized 10x DB' buffer, and sterilized ddH2O to a total volume of 1 L.
Supplement with 1 mL of sterilized 2 M MgCl2 and 1 mL of sterilized 1 M CaCl2.
Store the PS:DB medium at 4 °C.
Prepare the calcein-AM stock solution by adding 50 µL of DMSO to 50 µg of calcein-AM in the plastic container supplied by the manufacturer.
Store the calcein-AM stock at -20 °C.
Streak E. coli B/r from a frozen stock stored at -80 °C onto an LB agar plate.
Incubate the LB agar plate with streaked E. coli B/r overnight at 37 °C to obtain single colonies.
Inoculate a single colony of E. coli B/r into 2 mL of LB medium.
Incubate the inoculated LB medium in a roller drum or shaker at 37 °C overnight.
Bring the overnight E. coli culture to room temperature.
Inoculate amoebae from a frozen stock kept at -80 °C into 750 µL of the overnight E. coli culture using a wooden stick.
Immediately add 700 µL of the amoebae-E. coli mixture onto a Glucose Yeast Peptone (GYP) plate.
Spread the culture evenly on the surface of the GYP plate by tilting it back-and-forth and side-to-side as needed.
Place the GYP plate with agar facing up in a high-humidity box.
Fill the bottom container of the box with approximately 25 mL of water.
Drill several 0.5 cm-diameter holes through the flooring of the top container to allow moisture movement from the water reservoir to the top container.
Stack the top container onto the bottom container containing the GYP plate.
Incubate the GYP plate and box at 22 °C for 4 - 5 days until amoeba spores are observed growing near the surface of the plate.
Store plates with agar side facing up at 4 °C after observing spore growth, which can remain viable for several weeks.
After 3 - 4 days of incubation, observe zones of clearing within the bacterial lawn indicating the onset of amoeba sporulation.
Observe small amoebae spores above the plate surface after 4 - 5 days of incubation.
Sweep a sterile 1 mL pipette tip parallel to the surface of the plate to collect spores from half of a 10 cm Petri dish.
Avoid touching the tip to the surface of the agar plate during collection.
Resuspend amoebae by immersing pipette tip into 1 mL of PS medium and gently pipetting up and down.
Transfer inoculated mixture into a 250-mL flask containing 25 mL of PS medium supplemented with antibiotic-antimycotic solution at 0.25x concentration.
Grow amoebae axenically at 22 °C in a rotating shaker at 100 rpm.
For virulence assay, grow cells to an OD600 of 0.2 to 0.5.
If cells have grown to a higher density, dilute culture back in PS medium to an OD600 of 0.05 or lower and grow back to an OD600 of 0.2 to 0.5.
Pick a single colony of P. aeruginosa from an LB plate.
Inoculate the picked colony into a 2 mL PS:DB culture.
Grow overnight at 37 °C to saturation.
Dilute overnight culture 1:100 or 1:1,000 into a 6 cm-diameter Petri dish using PS:DB.
Shake the culture on a benchtop rotator set at 100 rpm at 37 °C.
Harvest cultures at specific time points to ensure reproducibility.
Prepare an agar pad as described in section 4 approximately 30 min to 1 h prior to assessing virulence.
Remove the liquid medium from the Petri dish when isolating surface-attached cells.
Wash immediately with 1 mL of DB buffer to remove planktonic cells.
Proceed immediately to step 5.1 after washing to isolate surface-attached cells.
Transfer 10 µL of the culture from the Petri dish to a clean Petri dish for isolating planktonic cells.
Proceed immediately to step 5.1 after transferring planktonic cells.
Microwave 50 mL of 1% (w/v) agar in DB buffer in a 250 mL flask until clumps disappear, mixing every 20 s.
Cool the molten agar by placing it in preheated 55 °C water bath for 15 min.
Add 15 µL of calcein-AM stock solution to 15 mL of molten agar in a conical tube.
Mix gently by inverting the tube 4 - 5 times.
Pour the molten agar mixture on top of a 12 cm x 10 cm glass plate.
Allow the agar to solidify for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Cut the solidified agar pad into smaller 1.5 cm x 1.5 cm sections using a metal ruler placed over a printed grid.
Keep the gel hydrated in a humid box until it is ready for use.
Add 10 μL of amoeba cells to surface-attached bacteria from step 3.4.
Mix 10 µL of amoeba cells with 10 µL of planktonic bacteria from step 3.5.
Place the 1.5 cm x 1.5 cm calcein-AM agar pad on top of the bacteria-amoeba mixture using a quick smooth motion.
Remove excess liquid by gently pipetting out any remaining liquid surrounding the agar pad.
Allow the Petri dish to dry for 20 min at room temperature.
Cover the Petri dish with a lid.
Incubate the immobilized amoeba-bacteria mixture at room temperature for an additional 40 min.
Image amoebae using a fluorescence microscope capable of acquiring brightfield and green fluorescence images.
Use green fluorescence protein (GFP) filters with 0.3 numerical aperture objective to image the amoebae.
Use 474/27 nm excitation filter and 525/45 nm emission filter for green fluorescence imaging.
Adjust acquisition times for the phase contrast channel to limit phototoxicity.
Optimize the dynamic range of image intensities for phase contrast.
Use 100 - 200 ms exposures for phase contrast if possible.
Keep exposure and instrument settings unchanged throughout the experiment.
Acquire images for at least 100 amoeba cells.
Adjust acquisition times for the GFP channel to limit phototoxicity.
Optimize the dynamic range of image intensities for GFP fluorescence.
Use 100 - 200 ms exposures for GFP fluorescence if possible.
Open the phase contrast image file in ImageJ by clicking File | Open and selecting the image.
Adjust the threshold by clicking on Image | Analysis | Threshold.
Select only the intensity peak by adjusting lower and upper thresholds.
Convert the image to binary by clicking Process | Binary | Make Binary.
Fill holes by selecting Process | Binary | Fill Holes.
Ensure that the Area and Mean gray value boxes are checked in Analyze | Set Measurements.
Measure the approximate size of amoebae using the oval tool on the main toolbar.
Click Analyze | Measure and note the area of representative amoebae.
Create masks for the amoebae by clicking Analyze | Analyze Particles.
Enter the area in the size box that will include the amoebae but exclude the bacteria.
Select Masks in the Show option dropdown menu bar.
Check the Add to Manager box and click OK.
Open the fluorescence image using File | Open and selecting the appropriate file.
Select all the regions in the ROI Manager by holding down the Shift Key and clicking on each region in the list.
Click the Measure button in the ROI Manager.
Copy the fluorescence values for each amoeba into a spreadsheet program.
Calculate the host killing index by taking the average of all fluorescence values.
